- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥3% from prior high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% based on sentiment decay.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and news volume remains high, model overcorrects downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence with true trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period rallies (last 5–7 days of true outcome); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is rising and news volume >2.5.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is low, model underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% downward buffer to forecast.
